A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELiC research, with the same main sections and Supplementary Material A–H. All 16 pages of each version provide readable text, equations, figures and tables, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original compression, runtime and ablation experiments on Ford and SemanticKITTI in Section 5, with additional runtime analyses and qualitative results in the supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains the original Ford and SemanticKITTI experiments, including Tables 1–5, supplementary runtime comparisons and per-point bit-allocation results.

M1.justification: The Morton hierarchy, cross-bit-depth feature propagation, BoE selection, training loss and coding procedures remain unchanged. Asynchronous arithmetic encoding was already described in v1 Supplement E; v2 expands its explanation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ford and SemanticKITTI for LiDAR geometry compression, with the same bit-depth coverage and qualitative examples. No dataset, task or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain G-PCCv30, RENO, RENO-Large, Unicorn and TopNet. Draco also remains in the supplementary rate-distortion curves in Fig. S5. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same sequence splits, quantization, training budget, model configurations and evaluation metrics. The new supplementary hardware statement and clarification that main-paper timings exclude asynchronous encoding disclose reporting scope without revising previously stated settings.

E4.justification: The BoE ablations, Morton sorting comparison, asynchronous-encoding analysis, parameter-efficiency comparison and bit-allocation case studies already appear in v1. V2 retains their questions, comparisons and evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The reporting of per-frame average runtimes is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and S1–S3 and the result figures retain their values and findings. For example, ELiC's average encoding/decoding times remain 0.121/0.111 seconds, and ELiC-Large's Ford D1 BD-Rate remains -26.54% relative to G-PCCv30.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20 and their mathematical reasoning are retained. Supplement C's description of duplicated parent coordinates and explicit conventional convolution weights clarify existing operations without introducing or revising a definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and compression/runtime claims for Morton order, cross-bit-depth propagation and BoE. The updated code-release statement does not change the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sparse-level compression gains, weaker performance at lower bit-depths and limitations of the fixed 4+4 factorization remain unchanged. The expanded CPU/GPU waiting explanation restates the existing rationale for asynchronous scheduling.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the future code/model release promise with reported availability of code and pretrained models, and Supplement C points to morton.py. Supplements D–E explicitly identify the runtime hardware and clarify that main-paper timings exclude asynchronous encoding. These improve access and reproducibility information without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: The same 42 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Supplement D's added 'sparse-tensor-based' qualifier makes an already established context explicit.

P1.justification: V2 corrects the author email domain and 'Abberation Studies' heading, standardizes capitalization and equation references, and expands a few supplementary explanations. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Fig. 1 adjusts the horizontal plotting margin, Fig. S1 revises the decoding output annotation, and Fig. S2 restyles explanatory labels. Supplementary tables receive small formatting and placement adjustments, with local text reflow; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 provides more actionable reproducibility guidance through its reported code/model availability, morton.py pointer and explicit timing scope. Small textual and visual corrections also improve clarity. The method, experimental evidence and conclusions remain unchanged, so the supported overall improvement is limited.
